tooltip.create_fire_control.fire_control: Two-axis stabilization
Stabilizes bound physical bearings in traverse and elevation and enforces elevation limits.
Head aim and gun sight
Aims the gun at the view reticle; the sight supports thermal imaging and mouse-wheel zoom.
Binding
Use a Create wrench to bind the bearings, seat, cannon mount, and remote weapon stations.
Remote head aim
Accepts only an active normal or advanced controller bound to a DriveByWire hub on this vehicle.
Ballistic solution

Identifies CBC, CBC: Modern Warfare, and compatible Mianbao cannon ammunition, barrel, and muzzle velocity, then calculates lead and elevation from _carrier motion, target motion, range, gravity, and drag_.
Sight, thermal, and camera
Provides sight entry and exit, continuous mouse-wheel zoom, thermal imaging, third-person aim height, and reticle offsets. Sight and thermal modes can also be switched by wireless or remote inputs.
Anti-tank missiles
Binds multiple Mianbao anti-tank launchers for _round-robin loaded-launcher selection, single-shot triggering, and flight guidance_; each launcher can supply a Head Aim direction anchor.
Radar and air defense

Scans physical structures and renders a radar HUD, cycles and locks targets, and fires air-defense missiles. Range, upper/lower coverage, minimum target speed, proximity range, and fuze safety are configurable.
Aircraft weapon system

Binds aircraft radar, missile racks, and rocket pods for unified _target cycle, radar lock, weapon selection, single fire, or salvo fire_. Infrared dogfight missiles need no radar; other air-to-air weapons use radar. AGMs and laser weapons use electro-optical targets.
Electro-optical pod

Provides an independently stabilized pod view, thermal imaging, and ground lock; controls pod traverse/elevation and guides AGMs and laser weapons. A cannon mount can follow pod line of sight with separate elevation limits.
Wireless and remote inputs
Create Redstone Links and normal/advanced Drive By Wire controllers can map sight, thermal, optical lock, anti-tank/air-defense/aircraft fire, radar target, weapon selection, and pod functions.
Structure and control settings

Configures stabilization and head aim, traverse/elevation speed and reversal, elevation limits, three structure offsets, hidden bearing heads, third-person view, radar HUD placement, and missile-fuze parameters.
tooltip.create_fire_control.connected_di: A tileable _independent radar, turret, automatic-weapon, and cruise-missile control terminal_.
Construction and binding

Adjacent panels facing the same way merge and share settings. Use a _Create Wrench_ on any panel, then bind radar bearings, physical bearings, cannon mounts, air-defense launchers, cruise/VLS launchers, or a forward indicator.
Radar and map

Uses a mechanical-bearing radar to track entities, physical structures, and incoming missiles, displaying position, velocity, and type. _Detection range, map update interval, and map resolution_ are configurable.
Targets and manual operation

Click the screen to select or clear targets, switch cannon/air-defense/cruise categories, designate a map aim point, and fire. It displays available weapons, missile types, and cruise-missile telemetry.
Bearings and cannons

Pairs multiple traverse bearings, elevation bearings, and cannon mounts by structure topology, applying _tracking, elevation limits, ballistic lead, and firing pulses_. Speed, reversal, and firing range are configurable.
Automatic attack

Automatically selects creatures or physical structures in range, drives an available turret, and advances after invalid or timed-out targets. Configure _maximum cannon range and own-structure clearance_ before enabling it.
Air defense and interception

Fires air-defense missiles manually or automatically intercepts incoming cruise, VLS, air-to-ground, and top-attack missiles with cannons or interceptors, with defense range, proximity distance, fuze safety, and duplicate-engagement prevention.
Cruise missiles and VLS
Recognizes eight cruise and ground-missile types and supports a radar target or map coordinate, missile selection, single-target launch, _multi-target salvo_, and in-flight telemetry.
Opening settings
_Sneak-right-click with an empty hand_ on any panel. Automatic modes require complete radar, bearing, and weapon bindings plus safe range settings.

create_fire_control.ponder.fire_control_: Planning the stabilized structure
The horizontal physical bearing is the yaw drive: its child structure is the turret.
Install the pitch bearing on the turret. Its child structure is the cannon or sensor head.
Required hierarchy: hull → yaw bearing → turret → pitch bearing → cannon. Assemble both bearings before testing.
Binding devices with the Create Wrench
First, right-click the Fire-control Computer with a Create Wrench to enter binding mode.
Blue outlines are compatible, unbound modules. Keep holding the wrench and right-click the module you need.
Red outlines are already bound to this computer. Bearings are auto-classified by placement and can be reassigned in Bound Devices.
Bind at least: yaw bearing, pitch bearing, operator seat, and an assembled cannon mount or supported ground-vehicle missile launcher.
Configuring limits, speeds and direction
Open the computer GUI. Use Yaw Settings for traverse speed/offset and Pitch Settings for depression, elevation, speed and offset.
Depression and elevation are rigid limits relative to the turret. They also apply when stress power tries to drive past them.
Offsets move the controlled child structure around its bearing anchor. Adjust in 0.1-block steps and test at low speed.
If an axis turns away from the reticle, enable only that axis' Reverse option. Manual reverse overrides automatic direction detection.
Stabilizer and head-aim operation
Enable Stabilizer to isolate each controlled rotation axis from its parent structure.
Sit in the bound operator seat. Head Aim then drives the cannon aim point toward your reticle while respecting speed and pitch limits.
The cannon ray, not the player's body rotation, is the final aiming reference. First-person and unlocked Sable view remain stabilized.
Remote authorization only replaces who activates Head Aim. Seat optics, radar, locking and other seat functions remain available.
Scope, optical pod and thermal imaging
Bind an assembled cannon mount for the gun sight, or bind an electro-optical pod for an independently aimed sensor view.
While either optical view is open, use the mouse wheel to change magnification. Zoom eases smoothly and is remembered separately.
Bind input actions in Input Bindings: one action toggles the selected optical view, and Thermal toggles white-hot imaging. Pod thermal starts off.
Only one player can use a particular scope or pod at a time. Leaving the seat, dying, or losing the device safely closes the view.
Quick fault-finding checklist
Axis does not move: confirm the physical bearing is assembled, still bound, has a child structure, and its maximum speed is above zero.
Pitch runs away or reverses: verify the hierarchy, then toggle Pitch Reverse. Do not compensate by swapping depression/elevation signs.
Head Aim has no direction: bind an assembled cannon mount or supported ground-vehicle missile launcher and verify the operator is in the bound seat.
Recommended first test: low traverse speed, ±10° pitch limits, stabilizer on, head aim on. Expand limits only after both axes follow correctly.
